Higher RPM comes from audience demographics more than niche.

Two finance channels, same topics, different RPM. 

Cuz one pulls US/UK/Canada traffic, one pulls India/Philippines traffic.

US viewers generate $18-25 RPM.

 India viewers generate $2-6 RPM. 

Same content but 5x difference.

How to control this: Title and thumbnail in English obviously attracts English-speaking markets but topic selection matters more. 

"How to invest $10k" attracts US audience. 

"Budget investing tips" attracts international audience.

This way YOU choose your RPM.

data.raw_text:
Antique find of the day!!!!! In 1898, Hobson took temporary command of a coal ship called the Merrimac. His mission was bold and risky: sink the ship in the narrow entrance to Santiago Harbor in Cuba to block the Spanish fleet inside.
Before dawn on June 3, he and his small crew sailed into the harbor under heavy enemy fire. Spanish guns quickly damaged the ship’s steering, making it hard to control. Although Hobson managed to sink the Merrimac, it did not land in the best position to completely block the channel.
Hobson and his six crew members were captured but treated respectfully by Spanish Admiral Cervera.
While he was a prisoner of war in Cuba, American newspapers turned Hobson into a national hero. His picture appeared in papers across the country, often alongside dramatic stories about his bravery. Many people believed he had volunteered for what seemed like a suicide mission. Supporters even raised money to help his parents save their home from foreclosure.
When Hobson was released in a prisoner exchange on July 6, 1898, American soldiers cheered loudly as he passed by. Back home, he received countless invitations to give speeches. After having dinner with President William McKinley, he traveled west by train toward San Francisco and eventually the Philippines. At nearly every stop, crowds gathered to see him.
Hobson became famous not just for his courage, but also for his charm. He often greeted admirers—especially young women—with enthusiastic kisses. Newspapers loved it. During a time when sensational journalism was growing in popularity, Hobson became a full-fledged celebrity and was even nicknamed “the most kissed man in America.”
This stereo view card has a rare picture of this man!
